article_title: Help! I Need Somebody: A Systematic Review of Academic Help-Seeking Among Pre-Service Teachers
citation: Navarro-Ibáñez, M., Balladares, J., Sprovera, I., Manaut, C., & Infante, M. (2026). Help! I Need Somebody: A Systematic Review of Academic Help-Seeking Among Pre-Service Teachers. Educational Psychology Review, 38, 115. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-026-10208-6
title: AHS as a socially embedded regulatory process within self-regulated learning
description: The review proposes an integrated conceptualization of academic help-seeking as a contextually and motivationally influenced regulatory process rather than a stable individual disposition. It argues that "help-seeking has a strong social component, as it heavily depends on the context and environment to encourage or discourage students from seeking help", and offers "a more integrated conceptualization of AHS as a socially embedded regulatory process within self-regulated learning". In teacher education, this framing highlights the relational nature of AHS and its potential implications for professional identity development.
requirements: Conceptualizing AHS within social-cognitive self-regulated learning frameworks rather than as a trait-like disposition
constraints: The review presents this as an integrative conceptualization suggested by the evidence, not as a directly tested model
target_learners: preservice teachers in teacher education programs
examples: The review synthesizes 32 empirical studies of AHS in preservice teachers to support this conceptualization
key_sources: Navarro-Ibáñez, M., Balladares, J., Sprovera, I., Manaut, C., & Infante, M. (2026). Help! I Need Somebody: A Systematic Review of Academic Help-Seeking Among Pre-Service Teachers. Educational Psychology Review, 38, 115. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-026-10208-6

article_title: Design and Validation of a Questionnaire to Measure Research Skills: Experience with Engineering Students
citation: Cobos Alvarado, F., Peñaherrera León, M., & Ortiz Colon, A. M. (2016). DESIGN AND VALIDATION OF A QUESTIONNAIRE TO MEASURE RESEARCH SKILLS: EXPERIENCE WITH ENGINEERING STUDENTS. Journal of Technology and Science Education. http://dx.doi.org/10.3926/jotse.227
title: AHABI: a 20-item self-rated questionnaire for measuring undergraduate research skills
description: The AHABI (Self-rated skills for research-based learning) is a self-administered Likert-scale questionnaire measuring research skills in university students. It consists of 20 items rated from 1 (strongly disagree) to 5 (strongly agree), developed because of a shortage of instruments for research skills: "The shortage of these instruments led to the creation of the scale of 'Self-rated skills for research-based learning' (AHABI)". It was validated with 150 basic-cycle engineering students and takes about 20 minutes to complete.
requirements: Administered as a self-completed questionnaire during regular class sessions with the researcher present giving instructions
constraints: Validated with basic-cycle engineering students aged 16 to 27 in Ecuador; the authors propose it as a starting point for studies in other knowledge areas
target_learners: undergraduate engineering students in the basic cycle
examples: Applied to 150 students (75.3% men, 24.7% women) enrolled in Physics, Differential Calculus, General Chemistry I and General Chemistry groups
key_sources: Cobos Alvarado, F., Peñaherrera León, M., & Ortiz Colon, A. M. (2016). DESIGN AND VALIDATION OF A QUESTIONNAIRE TO MEASURE RESEARCH SKILLS: EXPERIENCE WITH ENGINEERING STUDENTS. Journal of Technology and Science Education. http://dx.doi.org/10.3926/jotse.227

article_title: Evaluating the Effects of Mental Health e-Learning on the Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices of Primary Healthcare Professionals in Mali. A Pilot Study.
citation: Mroueh Lara, Bruand Pierre‐Emile, Poudiougou Oumar, Kleinebreil Line, Fall Ndao Amy, Moussaoui Driss, Preux Pierre‐Marie, Bagayoko Cheick Oumar, Boumediene Farid. (2025). Evaluating the Effects of Mental Health e‐Learning on the Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices of Primary Healthcare Professionals in Mali. A Pilot Study. Early Intervention in Psychiatry. https://doi.org/10.1111/eip.70001
title: AHRQ knowledge transfer framework (creation and distillation, diffusion and dissemination, organisational adoption and implementation)
description: The article uses the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality framework (Nieva et al. 2005) to frame the challenge of moving evidence into practice in Mali. It states that "Knowledge transfer in the AHRQ model (Nieva et al. 2005) includes three major stages: (1) knowledge creation and distillation, (2) diffusion and dissemination, and (3) organisational adoption and implementation." Knowledge creation translates research into actionable products such as practice guidelines; diffusion works through key opinion leaders and organisations; the final stage embeds evidence-based practice into routine care.
requirements: A synthesis of scientific information on knowledge transfer, social marketing, social and organisational innovation, and behaviour change, as the article describes the framework's basis
target_learners: primary healthcare professionals in low- and middle-income countries
target_learning_goals: transfer of evidence-based mental health knowledge and practices into primary care routine practice
examples: The e-learning platform itself is presented as the knowledge creation and distillation product, with partnerships (Santé Sud, FMOS, CERTES, WASP, UNFM) serving diffusion and dissemination.
